title: Horizontal filtration of the cone of a first-quadrant total map
statement: Let $C$ be abelian [def-sp-abelian] with totals for all first-quadrant bicomplexes [def-sp-double-complex-total], and let $f:A\to B$ be a morphism of first-quadrant bicomplexes. Extend total complexes by zero to integer degrees and set $M=\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Tot}(f))$. There is a decreasing subcomplex filtration $F$ [def-sp-filtration] of $M$. Its degreewise steps [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] satisfy $F^0M^n=M^n$ and $F^{n+2}M^n=0$ for every integer $n$. For every $p<0$, $H^n(\operatorname{gr}^p_FM)=0$ in every degree. For every $p\ge0$ and integer $n$, there is an isomorphism $H^n(\operatorname{gr}^p_FM)\cong H^{n-p}(\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{extend}(f^{p,\bullet})))$. No quasi-isomorphism hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: First horizontal filtration and its graded complexes; column-cone refinement of the finite endpoint comparison argument.

proof.text: In degree n take the direct sum of source terms A^(h,n+1-h) and target terms B^(h,n-h) with h>=p. Compose their diagonal inclusions with the source and target cone inclusions. Their image is the p-th subobject. The differential preserves or raises h: the source block is minus its total differential, the target block its total differential, and the off-diagonal f preserves h. Thus the restricted maps give subcomplexes; uniqueness through the monic inclusion proves square zero and compatibility. Inclusion of index sets gives an antitone filtration.

source.place: First horizontal filtration and its graded complexes; column-cone refinement of the finite endpoint comparison argument.

proof.text: All summands have horizontal index >=0, so step 0 is the entire cone. In degree n the source index is at most n+1 and the target index at most n. Therefore step n+2 vanishes. If n<-1 the cone object is zero, so both assertions remain true even when n+2<=0. For p<0 successive subcomplex steps are both the whole complex; their quotient is zero.

source.place: First horizontal filtration and its graded complexes; column-cone refinement of the finite endpoint comparison argument.

proof.text: For p>=0 the quotient of successive steps retains exactly the horizontal index p. Put k=n-p and e=(-1)^p. Its source and target blocks have differentials -e*d_A and e*d_B and its off-diagonal block is f^p. Multiply source summands in degree n by e^(k+1) and target summands by e^k. The successive scalars differ by e, and the source scalar in degree n equals the target scalar in degree n+1. These invertible scalars give a chain isomorphism to the integer column cone reindexed by n-p, including its degree -1 source summand. Apply the homology functor to obtain the asserted isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem firstQuadrant_vertical_cone_filtration {A B : HomologicalComplex₂ C (ComplexShape.up ℕ) (ComplexShape.up ℕ)} (f : A ⟶ B) : ∃ F : DecreasingFiltration (CochainComplex.mappingCone (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (total.map f (ComplexShape.up ℕ)) ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)), (∀ n : ℤ, F.complexStep 0 n = ⊤ ∧ F.complexStep (n + 2) n = ⊥) ∧ (∀ p n : ℤ, p < 0 → IsZero ((F.gradedPiece p).homology n)) ∧ (∀ p n : ℤ, 0 ≤ p → Nonempty ((F.gradedPiece p).homology n ≅ (CochainComplex.mappingCone (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (f.f p.toNat) ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)).homology (n - p)))
